messages:
Mariam: Quick sync — I sketched an approach for per-request cost memoization + stitching to avoid double-counting when requests flow through multiple enrichment stages and retries. Posting the gist, want quick gut-checks.
Evan: nice, can you summarize the invariants?
Mariam: sure. invariants: 1) each external request has a stable request_id propagated, 2) every enrichment stage reports only the marginal cost as cost_delta, 3) a memo store keyed by (request_id, stage) keeps observed cost_deltas, 4) stitcher reads memo entries and sums unique deltas to produce canonical billed cost, 5) retries dedupe via idempotency key + TTL.
Joel: looks sane. where does the memo live? in-process cache or central store?
Mariam: tradeoffs: local LRU reduces latency but can miss across pods -> central Redis/rocksdb recommended for correctness. propose: local LRU (1000 entries) as fast path, Redis as source-of-truth. writes to both async; read first local then redis.
Sam: how do we handle fanout where multiple stages run in parallel and emit the same cost? e.g., two microservices both call same model and both record cost_delta.
Mariam: good point. we plan to canonicalize stage ids (service:op) and use exact (request_id, canonical_stage) key. If two replicas both record cost for same canonical_stage, only first write wins (SETNX semantics) and subsequent writes return existing value. we attach a small vector: {cost_delta, source_node, timestamp, checksum} so stitcher can detect conflicts.
Evan: what about envelope bloat? adding memo keys to envelopes increases payload size and network cost.
Mariam: we avoid embedding full memo in every envelope. Enrichment stages write memo to store and emit only a tiny header: memo_ref=<request_id:stage> and cost_delta. stitcher will fetch memo entries lazily when building billable aggregates. optionally, gateway can eagerly fetch memo if needed for synchronous billing.
Joel: code-ish example of envelope shape?
Mariam: ```json
{"request_id":"r_12345","billing_hint":"tenant:acme","stage":"embed-lookup","cost_delta":12,"memo_ref":"r_12345:embed-lookup"}
```
Sam: sampling & retention: we can't keep full memo forever. what's TTL?
Mariam: default TTL 1h for most requests, configurable per-tier. For high-value customers we persist 7d. We keep small tombstones (marked deleted) for extra 24h to handle late-arriving stitch events.
Evan: how do we surface this in traces/metrics? need tags to correlate.
Mariam: add these trace/span tags: billing.request_id, billing.stage, billing.memo_hit (true/false), billing.cost_delta. Emit metrics: billing.memo_hits_total, billing.memo_misses_total, billing.memo_conflicts_total. Also a per-tenant gauge for in-flight memo size.
Joel: failure modes? if Redis is down we might undercount or overcount.
Mariam: fallback plan: if memo store unavailable, stages emit cost_delta + best-effort idempotency header. downstream stitcher will attempt dedupe by comparing checksums; we might accept higher error margin. Also instrument a rollout toggle so we can disable memoization per-service if instability detected.
Sam: what about sampling: for large volumes maybe we only memoize 1/N requests to reduce storage. how would that interact with stitcher?
Mariam: stitcher will use sampling flags. If memoized=false we mark those events and billing will extrapolate from sampled population. need to surface confidence intervals in billing UI.
Evan: ops questions: Redis capacity, eviction policy?
Mariam: use Redis with LFU eviction on smaller tier, and a dedicated RocksDB-backed store for enterprise with SSD persistence. For Redis sizing estimate: avg memo entry ~120 bytes, peak QPS 50k -> with TTL 1h => 50k*3600*120B ~ 21GB. so many customers will need sharding / dedicated clusters.
telemetry-bot: deploy: memo-store feature flag enabled in staging at 2026-03-15T22:00Z.
Mariam: next steps: write short RFC doc with these tradeoffs + pseudo-APIs (SetMemo, GetMemo, ClaimMemo) and a small integration test that simulates retries and fanout. Volunteers for RFC? @Evan @Joel
Evan: I can take the API sketch.
Joel: I can mock load/size numbers and sample extrapolation formulas.
Mariam: awesome — I'll draft the RFC and ping the channel when ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
